nodes.description: FBXO43 (EMI2) binds the APC/C and holds its ubiquitin ligase activity in check during meiosis. In patient testis a homozygous nonsense allele removed the protein. Truncating and missense alleles both made FBXO43 less stable in transfected cells and broke its binding to APC3, the APC/C substrate-recognition subunit, while binding to APC2, APC6 and APC8 was kept. In Xenopus eggs, the C-terminal tail of EMI2 blocks the APC/C by occupying the APC10 site that the E2 enzyme Ube2S needs.

nodes.description: Reported in one man with two C-terminal missense variants. His spermatocytes completed meiosis, but his sperm had a raised rate of aneuploidy on FISH, together with poor chromatin condensation and histone retention. The missegregation itself happens in the meiotic divisions of spermatocytes; it is observed as aneuploidy in the sperm.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation Severity of FBXO43 Determines Spermatogenic Outcome and Informs Precision ART Strategies.
evidence.snippet: Missense variants (NM_001029860, p.Pro641Leu/p.Arg660Gln) in the macrozoospermia patient allowed completion of meiosis but led to severe sperm head enlargement, chromatin condensation defects, and markedly elevated aneuploidy, resulting in repeated ICSI failure.
